name: Lilliput Multi Cuisine Restaurant
signature_dish: Karimeen pollichathu and butter-garlic squid — the standout seafood plates
why_it_matters: The most-reviewed restaurant at Cherai Beach — around 4.5 on TripAdvisor across hundreds of reviews — and the spot locals name first when asked where to eat on the beach strip. The seafood is the draw: karimeen pollichathu, butter-garlic squid and tawa prawns, with a side of Chinese and tandoor for mixed groups.
insider_tip: Food can take 40-45 minutes at busy times — order early or come off-peak. The Ammachi (Kerala home-style) section is better than the multi-cuisine pages. Reasonable prices for the quality.
signature_address: Cherai-Munambam Beach Road, Cherai Beach, Vypin Island, Kochi, Kerala 683514

name: Chilliout Cafe Cherai Beach
signature_dish: Wood-fired thin-crust pizza and French crepes on the sand
why_it_matters: A beachfront palm-thatch cafe run by a Paris-origin owner, Chilliout is Cherai's go-to for French-leaning food — crepes, thin-crust pizza, barbecue — with vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options uncommon on this beach. Consistently ranked among Cherai's top two restaurants on TripAdvisor.
insider_tip: Sit on the beachside chairs for sunset. It is a touch pricier than the local Kerala places nearby — go for the pizza and crepes, which are what it does best, rather than Indian dishes.
signature_address: Cherai Beach (beachfront), Vypin Island, Kochi, Kerala 683514

name: Oceanview
area: Cheraibeach Road, beside Sea Lagoon, Cherai Beach
signature_dish: Catch-of-the-day grilled fish eaten 25 metres from the surf
why_it_matters: A simple sea-facing seafood place on Cheraibeach Road, barely 25 metres from the water, next to Sea Lagoon resort. Cherai's reputation is for sunsets over the Arabian Sea, and Oceanview is built around exactly that — fresh seafood eaten with the waves audible and the sun going down.
insider_tip: It is an evening place — go for dinner around sunset. There is a covered section if it drizzles. Cash and UPI; informal beach-shack service, so allow time.
signature_address: Cheraibeach Road, beside Sea Lagoon Resort, Cherai Beach, Vypin Island, Kochi, Kerala 683514

name: Spice Trails at Cherai Beach Resorts
signature_dish: Kerala seafood and sadya-style spreads in a backwater-and-beach resort setting
why_it_matters: The restaurant of Cherai Beach Resorts, the long-running property set where the backwater meets the beach. Spice Trails serves authentic Kerala dishes alongside international fare; the resort also runs an Oottupura local-cuisine outlet. A comfortable, sit-down option on a beach strip otherwise dominated by informal shacks.
insider_tip: Non-residents can dine here — call ahead in season. Ask for the Kerala fish curry and appam; the resort sits where the backwater opens to the sea, so request a water-facing table.
signature_address: Cherai Beach Resorts, Cherai-Munambam Road, Cherai Beach, Vypin Island, Kochi, Kerala 683514

name: Munambam Beach Fish Shacks
area: Munambam Beach, 4 km north of Cherai
signature_dish: Fresh-off-the-boat fish fried at informal stalls by the Munambam harbour
why_it_matters: Munambam, 4km north of Cherai at the tip of Vypin Island, is a working fishing harbour where the day's catch comes ashore. Informal stalls and small shacks near the landing fry fish straight off the boats — the cheapest, freshest seafood on this stretch, eaten where it is caught rather than in a tourist restaurant.
insider_tip: Go around the late-morning or evening boat landings for the freshest fish — stalls are informal and timing follows the catch, not a clock. Carry cash; this is a harbour-side, not a sit-down, experience.
signature_address: Munambam Beach, near the fishing harbour, Vypin Island, Kochi, Kerala 683516
